This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. The road to Manang doesnt make promises. It tests you first. I came during the monsoon when the mountain roads turned into mud, the cliffs crumbled without warning and every bend carried the possibility of a landslide. In Nepal’s Himalayas, the journey can be just as unforgiving as the mountains themselves. But some places are worth the risk. Manang, deep inside the Annapurna Conservation Area is one of them. The jeep road ends here. Beyond this point theres only one way forward, on foot. This is where the legendary Annapurna Circuit truly begins. Depending on your pace, the trek takes around 12 days, carrying you through some of the most breathtaking landscapes on Earth. I came in the off season. Fewer people, quieter trails, raw weather. And somehow it made the experience feel even more real. Sometimes the hardest roads lead to the places you will never forget.♥️ #manang #nepal #traveltiktok #mountains #annapurna
